title: Technology Decision Map
html:
This is a navigation summary, not an independent technology specification. Each linked ADR owns the decision, exceptions, rationale, and version policy. Every record listed below currently states accepted, with ADR-0014 partly superseded by ADR-0017; workspace tooling, the API runtime with composable modules and PostgreSQL support, generated SDK, web shell, documentation portal, and project-derivation tooling exist. Consult validation availability before running commands.

Selected directions

Governing decision Direction Important scope Current policy
ADR-0001 TypeScript 6.x; Node.js 24 LTS initial baseline; ESM Primary, not exclusive; exact compatible versions belong in tooling. Policy
ADR-0002 pnpm and pnpm workspaces Shared lockfile, workspace protocol, catalogs when useful; no dedicated task runner initially. Policy
ADR-0003 tsc, ESLint/typescript-eslint, Prettier, dependency-cruiser Non-mutating canonical validation and separate formatting command are implemented for current tooling. Policy
ADR-0004 Fastify; Pino for HTTP runtime logging Transport/infrastructure adapters do not define business-domain boundaries. Policy
ADR-0005 PostgreSQL pgvector is preferred when a suitable vector workload requires it, not enabled by default; AI access remains authorized through application capabilities. Policy
ADR-0006 Prisma ORM 7, Prisma Client, Prisma Migrate Parameterized SQL/TypedSQL and custom migrations remain available; complete physical schema comes from migrated PostgreSQL. Policy
ADR-0007 HTTP/JSON, TypeBox 1.x, generated OpenAPI 3.1.x initially, openapi-typescript and openapi-fetch Wire contracts, stable operation IDs, and TypeBox bootstrap configuration; client response revalidation is not automatic. Policy
ADR-0008 React 19.x, React Compiler when compatible, Vite 8.x, TanStack Router and Query Client-first SPA; URL, server, and local UI state have distinct owners; server rendering is requirement-driven. Policy
ADR-0009 Vitest, Testcontainers, Vitest Browser Mode with Playwright, Playwright Test Real migrated PostgreSQL; browser fidelity where relevant; no initial global coverage threshold. Policy
ADR-0010 OpenTelemetry traces/metrics, Pino logs, W3C Trace Context, OTLP Collector preferred when justified, not mandatory; no global backend/vendor or baseline browser instrumentation. Policy
ADR-0011 GitHub Actions and Renovate; available GitHub security capabilities Same validation as local development; immutable action pins; automerge off initially; CI does not select CD. Policy
ADR-0012 Locally verified JWT bearer access tokens for the first API Provider-independent issuer/audience/JWKS verification and stable application principal mapping; the foundation record does not select a concrete provider; accepted Teluni ADR-0024 does. Policy
ADR-0013 AGENTS.md hierarchy as the only agent instruction source Tool-specific files are thin discovery adapters only; currently a Gemini CLI setting. Policy
ADR-0014 Projects derived from Orion by Git ancestry with .orion/project.json provenance Fetch-only orion-upstream, reviewed upgrade merges, immutable commits instead of a release scheme. Policy
ADR-0017 Derived projects start from a clean baseline .orion/derivation.json separates shared, foundation-only, and project-owned content; initialization removes the reference implementation and foundation history and applies the project identity. Policy

Accepted Teluni product directions

The owner explicitly accepted the seven pending product ADRs on 2026-10-18, and ADR-0026 the same day under PH-21. ADR-0027 was accepted on 2026-10-19 under PH-22. These rows describe architectural choices, not installed dependencies, implemented product modules or qualified production capability. Concrete design and delivery evidence remain in the product plan.

Governing decision Accepted direction Current policy / remaining gate
ADR-0018 Shared PostgreSQL database/schema with explicit tenant ownership, scoped references and modular backend Architecture; concrete constraints, additional RLS evaluation and cross-tenant tests pending
ADR-0019 Immutable versioned publications and complete durable player activation/recovery Playback/sync; protocol and failure/power qualification pending
ADR-0020 Independent native Kotlin/Media3 Android TV player with durable local state Architecture; supported hardware, packaging, persistence and recovery tests pending
ADR-0021 Initial Debian/Compose host, HTTPS, private PostgreSQL and portable persistent media Operations; host/network/backup/restore and real-customer readiness pending
ADR-0023 Versioned declarative composition and typed catalogs in immutable publications Release policies; concrete schemas, rendering/storage and qualified interoperability pending
ADR-0024 Self-hosted Keycloak and server-managed human browser sessions, preserving ADR-0012 Identity/access; pinned-source assessment supports selection, actual provider/session integration pending
ADR-0025 Application-owned scoped standard/custom profiles and attributable consent-based support Identity/access; concrete authorization/session contracts and all IA cases pending
ADR-0026 Transactional email through a PostgreSQL outbox, an in-process dispatcher and a provider-neutral SMTP relay (nodemailer), at least once Invitation and email delivery design; accepted 2026-10-18 under PH-21; real sender/provider PH-17 and retention PH-13 pending
ADR-0027 Code-based device enrollment shaped like RFC 8628 and device-generated bearer credentials stored only as hashes, separate from human sessions Device enrollment design; accepted 2026-10-19 under PH-22; Android player PJ-12 and hardware PH-08 pending

Deliberately unresolved or conditional choices

  • The API's development/build convention is implemented. A dedicated task orchestrator, TypeScript project references, and advanced unused-code analysis are not initial requirements.
  • UI/design systems, styling, accessibility primitives, charts, grids, and forms depend on product needs. No general global-state library or full-stack web framework is selected by default.
  • GraphQL, tRPC, gRPC, rich SDK generators, and other-language clients require a concrete consumer or boundary. They do not replace the accepted interoperable API by implication.
  • Bearer access-token verification is implemented as shared API infrastructure under ADR-0012; Teluni accepts Keycloak and server-managed sessions through ADR-0024, while concrete session/refresh/revocation implementation and qualification remain pending. Other applications' authorization and tenancy choices and AI delegation mechanisms depend on their requirements. Existing security policies still apply.
  • Queue/messaging infrastructure, background-job infrastructure, cache, search, dedicated vector infrastructure, and object-storage providers are not global defaults. Introduce them only for demonstrated requirements. Teluni's transactional email uses the PostgreSQL outbox, in-process dispatcher and SMTP relay accepted in ADR-0026; that does not make them a general job or messaging platform.
  • Mobile and desktop stacks, deployment platform, application containerization, cloud provider, infrastructure as code, and continuous delivery are product/deployment decisions. Teluni has accepted its Android and initial Compose directions above; detailed tooling and operational readiness are not thereby supplied. Testcontainers does not select an application deployment platform.
  • Observability storage/vendors, error-reporting providers, alerting/paging, sampling rates, and retention depend on operational requirements. Do not introduce a provider abstraction solely to hide a vendor without a genuine responsibility.

Compatible version evolution follows the individual ADRs. These recorded baselines are not installed-version claims. Implementation progress belongs in normal work tracking and capability documentation, not new ADR statuses.
